@connorn-dev this is very good! Seems you are a natural on this, which is quite rare! Let's refine your specification a bit further now you have the core idea. 

As you noted above, we need to get data from Kaiaulu to be used on pm4py. Currently you can get the data via the notebook, but when we want to write inter-tool data pipelines, it is best we can provide said data via a `CLI` interface. Meaning, you can just run a `script` on the terminal to get a table out. The script mostly duplicates a portion of the notebook behavior, but it is more streamlined. 

Done this way, the Python code can just call Kaiaulu script from its side and the analysis continue from there. Therefore, your first checkbox is correct, but right after it I would add a second that says: `extend exec/github.R to allow exporting GitHub API event data`. 

Then expand your process section with some of the following: 

R packages can have a folder called `/exec`: https://stackoverflow.com/questions/52171091/using-exec-directory-in-r-packages-for-r-scripts-for-reproducible-research  and also https://r-pkgs.org/misc.html#other-directories 

Kaiaulu have a few, some still WIP in PRs. Here's the one relevant for you: https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/pull/301 you will want to expand it to also have a command to get event API data out. 

You can use as reference point the one Dao did: 

https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/blob/4df52d92fdbaae556e39cc56dd0ef6faf752b788/exec/mailinglist.R#L15-L34 

This code is part of the Pull Request for Mbox last session. You won't find on the master branch, but rather here: https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/pull/295/files

Much like you found functions on R/github.R being used in the GitHub API Notebook, Dao also expanded on R/mail.R in her PR: https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/blob/4df52d92fdbaae556e39cc56dd0ef6faf752b788/R/mail.R and also wrote her own Notebook explaining it: https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/blob/4df52d92fdbaae556e39cc56dd0ef6faf752b788/vignettes/download_mail.Rmd 

You can see here that her exec can be used to download data both from pipermail and mod_mbox, two different type of mail archives. You will be adding an event "endpoint" to github.R on PR 295 (meaning you will commit to that PR modifying it, instead of creating a new PR, but conforming to how Dao organized her code since it is the more current standard). 


This means that there are 3 files of interest as part of what will become your PR: 

* R/github.R (where the API functions reside. New capabilities will be added here as functions)
* exec/github.R a script that uses these functions and provide a CLI interface so it is callable by other scripts, or the user can use from the terminal if they do not know R 
* vignette/github_api_showcase.Rmd where the explanation of the capability is demonstrated 

At a minimum, any R package has the R folder, giving you new functions to analyze data. Best practice is that R packages also give you notebooks explaining how to use them, a bit like a manual. Then finally a few rare packages will offer you the `/exec` folder as a set of scripts.

Let me know if you have questions.

Hi Ryan, Thank you for the update. I think the issue specification is not quite there yet, and that in turn will affect the impact of what really your code is adding from a capability standpoint. I finally had some quiet time to spend looking through #323. So let me go in further detail here to explain how I would like you to approach creating specifications to help you navigate this capability for Kaiaulu. The first thing we need to do is confirm what we really want this Kaiaulu capability to be. The capability we want is to be able to download Pull Request data associated to developer interaction. On call, I mentioned a few times that when looking at developer conversation for Pull Requests, we have at least three ways I've seen interaction happening: 1. Conversation tab 2. Files changed tab 2.1 After reviews 2.2 After single line comments Now, the next step is consider why are they different. Aren't they just comments at the end of the day? Well, `Conversation` really is a comment as a standalone, much like this one I am using to communicate with you. The `Files changed tab` is different, because my comments are strictly about your code. In a `single line comment` review, they are simply the comment and the pointer to the code. In a `review` they come with a status, i.e. whether i reject or accept your current state of commits up to that point and I also group all single line comments under it. This nuance in the developer vs developer interaction is useful data. Having acknowledge that as my **objective and motivation** for this capability in Kaiaulu, what follows then is: 1. Does Kaiaulu already have this capability? If yes, what `permalink` can I place here linking to the function signature so I can easily find? Next, is what example endpoint can I paste here to show a data sample? For example in #323 you will find the following API example for the review endpoint: https://api.github.com/repos/sailuh/kaiaulu/pulls/295/reviews For each function, you can construct an url for that. Someone clicking this in firefox will get a preformatted json too to explore. From the top of my memory, Kaiaulu has 1. already in its master branch. Kaiaulu should have on the #330 the capability for 2.2. But we lack 2.1. 2. The second step is to ask yourself what else is out there? And how can I succinctly convey that in the issue specification as a section? Well, if I look at the docs: We can see there are at least 3 very convincing places I can confirm what else is out there. If we expand one of them: We can quickly eliminate endpoints that are POST. The ones that are `GET` that offer to list information we want to inspect the response object to see what information they offer. You have to annotate on your issue, not pasting the json screenshots, what data they offer so you can compare and leave documented here. Odds are that some of them are redundant, or some of the information we don't really care. However, if you don't summarize the data you can get, maybe as bullets, or a sample table, we won't be able to decide. For instance, in #330 we see diff_hunk is a useful information to have: We can find what code the comment was about. Understanding the data specifics is also needed, or you will be unable to find how you can inner join this data after converting json to tables. For example: ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/510cef57-b749-466b-81e3-ffef28d5a23c) ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e3cc30f3-0d68-4c72-bf42-269482f8523b) This screenshot is a fantastic example on how to convey that. However, these connections comes after you consider what data is available. Why am I emphasizing this? The PR you made is for the endpoint: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/comments?apiVersion=2022-11-28#list-review-comments-in-a-repository However, the comment of the two screenshots above says **the capability we are missing lives on the Review endpoint** (https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/issues/323#issuecomment-2533462925) and the screenshot above even shows exactly what the Review endpoint captures. Does the endpoint you used at the scope of the PR adds the missing information? Or it adds something else? Again, we need the bigger picture enumerated and properly organized on your issue specification to tell that apart. Here's a way I would do that. Building on my screenshot above of the 3 candidate places to look at for what information the Pull Request endpoints provided, I could make a bullet list: * Pull Requests * List Pull Requests: [Docs](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/pulls?apiVersion=2022-11-28#list-pull-requests) | Example URL | Permalink to Kaiaulu function signature if implemented * Information it provides (probably best to add the columns you would get out of this, but an overall idea can work to save time. Say, this endpoint being the comments under "Conversation tab" * Other endpoint * Other endpoint * Review Comments * List Review Comments in a Repository: [Docs](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/comments?apiVersion=2022-11-28#list-review-comments-in-a-repository) * List Review Comments on a Pull Request: [Docs](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/comments?apiVersion=2022-11-28#list-review-comments-on-a-pull-request) * Review Requests * Reviews * List Reviews for a Pull Request: [Docs](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/reviews?apiVersion=2022-11-28#list-reviews-for-a-pull-request) --------- In short, because I do not have the forest for the tree, I do not know if the function you implemented addresses the goal of this milestone. As you can see, there is absolutely no way we will converge on this if all our discussion and decision making happens on call without discussion and summarizing the decisions here. Take a step back, review the specification and we can decide if the endpoint you have is what is left to implement or if we need to add other endpoints. Let me know if you have any questions on how to update your specifications.

@carlosparadis I've gone through the current architecture section and Kaiaulu's functions and here's what I learned so far about the design: 

Kaiaulu is flexible in terms of customizing the intermediate steps to display the results you want. Example functions like the parse_gitlog() and parse_mbox() are used to extract data, turns them into raw data or JSON from git logs or mailing lists, and eventually turned into tables where it than can be utilized (Combined with other data, transformed, visualized, etc.). or examined.

Good in reproducibility. Project configuration files written in YAML stores project-specific information like which tools the project uses or where data files could be located. Someone else can produce the same results using the same settings that is given from it. Since the project config is simple, written in YAML, it can also be expanded upon as we innovate the project.

Kaiaulu is designed to feel familiar if you have used R before due to it being packaged like a standard R library so you can do things such as provide functions you can call, provide documentation explaining what each function does, and having example notebooks showing how to use them. It makes it easier for people who already know R and also helps beginners because the structure and workflow are already documented.

Kaiaulu is designed in a way to work with other tools. It uses tools like Perceval or Depends to gather more data about a project. We don't see these tools "working" but rather Kaiaulu wraps the tools functions calls, within its own function calls.
